docs.description: You will find here all the 3D models needed to make a costume of Leia on Lothal from Star Wars Rebels 12th episode of the second season: "A princess on Lothal". The only missing part is the Comlink as two great models are already proposed on thingiverse by others (links below). You will find the following elements: - Chestbox. There is no fixation modelled so you are free to choose how to attach it: glue on the fabric, magnets, etc. I personally recommend printing one or two more chest clips to glue at the top so you can clip the chestbox to the collar, and glue a magnet on the bottom to hold it with another magnet on the other side of the fabric. - Chest clips to print twice and to wear on the collar on both sides of the chestbox. - Back clips (one right and on left as they are not symmetric to themselves), to also wear on the collar... in the back. - A Belt box in two versions functional and non-functional. In the episode, it can be hardly seen and we can only guess the square recessed in it. The non-functional correspond to that. The functional box is in 3 parts (box, cover and belt clip), and is a slightly modified design acceptable given the lack of good pictures. Use some metallic wire or two sewing pins to attach the cover to the box thanks to the dedicated small holes. The size is designed to take standard size business cards. - A haircomb/hairclip, in 3 versions. The "basic" one allows you to glue attachement system you want such as a clasp. The "clip" contains something to slide in hairs (not test). The "comb" is a traditional hair comb, it should be strong enough, at least with ABS. - A belt buckle composed of 3 elements. Left/Right and the cover. The left part is to be glue to the cover (alignment pin/registration marks included). The right part can then slide in the left from the bottom. The left and right part are designed to use a 40mm wide belt/strap. Tests print in ABS (100% infill) have been able to withstand several kilograms of pulling force without breaking. You can make the belt/strap adjustable just like for a backpack by passing the strap in the side hole, around the dedicated loop and back again in the side hole and sew the extremity of the strap folded on itself so it can go off. I will try to add an example in the "makes". Sizes might need to be slightly adjusted to the wearer as this is based on cartoon character. Current size is for an average person. All parts are to be painted in a silver, if possible with blue hue. The round buttons on the chestbox should be done with a darker metallic (ex: gun metal), while recessed grooves/borders on all pieces (when present) should be dark grey to black. Regarding print settings, all models should already be in optimised orientation to minimise support and/or get best results. I print with brims, not raft. I recommend printing the chest/back clips, the belt buckles parts and the hair comp at 100% infill, 20% for the other files. Tolerances are already included in the models. Links for comlink models: - By Mooslug: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:491072 - By Machinimax: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3858035

docs.description: This is a Tarkin Town shed inspired by the TV show - Star Wars Rebels. It's not screen accurate... so if you're looking for that, move along; move along!!! I made the roof separate, so if you need to hide objective or miniatures inside, it's possible to do so. The door slides open almost completely... if you listen closely, you can the door go 'shhh'! This is the -low roof- version, I will upload a bit taller/different one soon. Print the roof and the door vertically, the braces laying flat. You might have to "shave off" some material from the braces ends so they fit better inside the holes I left for them in the roof and front wall. docs.description: Ruk Sindhi - Lothal, A prosperous port of Indus Civilization Lothal was inhabited during 3700 BCE and was a thriving trading port. Archaeologists believe that the city was a part of a major river system on the ancient trade route from Sindh to Saurashtra in Gujarat. The most architecturally sophisticated part of Lothal was its dockyard, which provided berthing facilities for the ships. Discovery of a rectangular dockyard at Lothal indicates that the people had maritime trade relations with other civilizations. رڪ سنڌي، سنڌو سڀيتا جو خوشحال بندرگاهه لوٿل

docs.creator: Patrick LeBrun (BwetDude)
docs.description: This is a Tarkin town HOUSE inspired by the TV show - Star Wars Rebels. It's not screen accurate... so if you're looking for that, move along; move along!!! I made the main roof separate, so if you need to hide objective or miniatures inside, it's possible to do so. You have 2 choices of "short" walls and 3 for the "long" one. Basically with or without windows. And square building or one with a round vestibule. The you can remove the doors to this model, it didn't have enough space to slide them with the window and the front curved wall became too thin when I tried to give it space so the door could slide open. - sorry. Print the roof, the walls and the doors vertically. The round wall vertically but upside down to save on supports. The awnings pointing upwards should require next to no support also. I made a set of pegs that are 0,5mm less than the holes... so technically they should fit snug. Same for the top roof rectangular tenons. I may add a second floor to this house in the future and maybe a tower... If you find the wall too bare, you can slap 'greebles' to you linking on them. I didn't want to force hard to print and paint details that could be crafted afterwards. Like the CC License states, print and have fun, don't sell, if you print and feel satisfied with the result, you can send a few 'credits' my way, I'll use them to support 3D designer's Patreons... or to build an actual workshop if the flow is overwhelming!! haha.
